pr.title: perf(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): masked pair program for homed weights from expected_m 128 on sm_107a
pr.body:
The batch DeepGEMM FP8 Cake family has three serving programs for packed-UE8M0 weights on 212-SM sm_107a. The first is the whole-GPU M32 serving program. The second is its locality-domain twin, used for weights homed by `localize_weights`. The third is the masked pair program for large expected_m. This PR routes homed weights to the pair program from expected_m 128 instead of 160. The baseline is the previous Cake route for homed weights, which is the twin.

NVIDIA VR200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs, dies 106/106), driver 620.70.06, memory at 4752 MHz, CUDA 13.5. B=64 homed weights of (N, K) = (4096, 7168). CUPTI device time, CUDA graph replay, cold L2; medians over 6 rounds; speedup = previous time / new time (per-round range). Uneven rows draw each group's count as int(em x U(0.7, 1.3)).

| mask | expected_m | M | previous Cake (twin) us | this PR (pair) us | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| even | 128 | 128 | 274.2 | 247.1 | 1.110 (1.108-1.111) |
| even | 144 | 256 | 334.2 | 256.0 | 1.306 (1.304-1.307) |
| even | 159 | 256 | 335.2 | 256.5 | 1.307 (1.305-1.308) |
| uneven | 128 | 256 | 299.3 | 250.4 | 1.195 (1.194-1.196) |
| uneven | 144 | 256 | 331.5 | 253.2 | 1.309 (1.307-1.311) |
| uneven | 159 | 256 | 371.6 | 255.6 | 1.454 (1.450-1.458) |

The family also ships whole-GPU serving programs on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. The twins and the pair program are sm_107a only.

+"""On the device: the locality domain an SM reports is the die whose memory it
+reads faster.
+
+One CTA per SM chases a random chain of dependent L2-missing loads through memory
+of die 0 and through memory of die 1 (one :func:`flashinfer.cake_locality.
+split_empty` allocation) and times each chase with ``%globaltimer``. Each SM
+must read the memory of the domain in its ``%locality_domain_id`` register
+faster than the other die's memory, by a margin, and the SMs of each domain must
+match :func:`flashinfer.cake_locality.sm_table`. On sm_107a boards with 106/106
+and 100/112 SMs per die, at 3186 and 4752 MHz memory clocks, the per-SM ratio
+of the other die's load latency to the own die's was 1.47-1.57 (305-334 ns own,
+471-500 ns other); the test asserts at least :data:`MIN_REMOTE_OVER_LOCAL`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import statistics
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from flashinfer import cake_locality as cl
+
+# Per SM, median remote load latency over median local load latency.
+MIN_REMOTE_OVER_LOCAL = 1.2
+# Dependent loads per chase, launches per chase order, attempts per launch to
+# place one CTA on every SM.
+STEPS = 1024
+LAUNCHES = 3
+ATTEMPTS = 4
+# One chain node every STRIDE_WORDS 4-byte words (256 bytes).
+STRIDE_WORDS = 64
+
+_CHASE_SOURCE = r"""
+#include <cstdint>
+
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/container/tensor.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/error.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/extra/c_env_api.h>
+#include <tvm/ffi/function.h>
+
+constexpr int kStrideWords = 64;
+
+__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned long long GlobalTimer() {
+  unsigned long long t;
+  asm volatile("mov.u64 %0, %%globaltimer;" : "=l"(t));
+  return t;
+}
+
+// Thread 0 of CTA c stores (smid, locality domain, supplemental flag, ns of the
+// chase through die 0's half, ns through die 1's half) at row c. order 1 chases
+// die 1's half first.
+__global__ void __launch_bounds__(32, 1)
+    ChaseKernel(const unsigned* __restrict__ half0, const unsigned* __restrict__ half1,
+                const int* __restrict__ starts, int steps, int order, long long* out) {
+  if (threadIdx.x != 0) return;
+  unsigned smid, domain, supplemental;
+  asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(smid));
+  asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%locality_domain_id;" : "=r"(domain));
+  asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%locality_domain_supplemental_sm;" : "=r"(supplemental));
+  long long ns[2];
+  unsigned sink = 0;
+  for (int i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
+    int side = order ? 1 - i : i;
+    const unsigned* p = side ? half1 : half0;
+    unsigned index = static_cast<unsigned>(starts[blockIdx.x]);
+    unsigned long long t0 = GlobalTimer();
+    for (int s = 0; s < steps; ++s) {
+      index = __ldcg(p + static_cast<size_t>(index) * kStrideWords);
+    }
+    sink ^= index;
+    ns[side] = static_cast<long long>(GlobalTimer() - t0);
+  }
+  long long* row = out + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * 6;
+  row[0] = smid;
+  row[1] = domain;
+  row[2] = supplemental;
+  row[3] = ns[0];
+  row[4] = ns[1];
+  row[5] = sink;
+}
+
+void Chase(tvm::ffi::TensorView chain, int64_t half_words, tvm::ffi::TensorView starts,
+           int64_t steps, int64_t order, tvm::ffi::TensorView out) {
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(chain.ndim() == 1 && chain.size(0) == 2 * half_words);
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(starts.ndim() == 1 && out.ndim() == 2 && out.size(1) == 6);
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(out.size(0) == starts.size(0));
+  DLDevice device = chain.device();
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(cudaSetDevice(device.device_id) == cudaSuccess);
+  int smem = 0;
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&smem, cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin,
+                                        device.device_id) == cudaSuccess);
+  // Each CTA asks for an SM's whole opt-in shared memory, so no two share an SM.
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(cudaFuncSetAttribute(ChaseKernel, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize,
+                                      smem) == cudaSuccess);
+  cudaStream_t stream =
+      static_cast<cudaStream_t>(TVMFFIEnvGetStream(device.device_type, device.device_id));
+  const unsigned* base = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned*>(
+      static_cast<const char*>(chain.data_ptr()) + chain.byte_offset());
+  ChaseKernel<<<static_cast<unsigned>(starts.size(0)), 32, static_cast<size_t>(smem), stream>>>(
+      base, base + half_words,
+      reinterpret_cast<const int*>(static_cast<const char*>(starts.data_ptr()) +
+                                   starts.byte_offset()),
+      static_cast<int>(steps), static_cast<int>(order),
+      reinterpret_cast<long long*>(static_cast<char*>(out.data_ptr()) + out.byte_offset()));
+  const cudaError_t status = cudaGetLastError();
+  TVM_FFI_ICHECK(status == cudaSuccess) << cudaGetErrorString(status);
+}
+
+TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC(chase, Chase);
+"""
+
+
+def _require_table() -> tuple[int, cl.SmTable]:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required")
+    device = torch.cuda.current_device()
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device) != (10, 7):
+        pytest.skip("Cake locality domains need sm_107a")
+    from flashinfer.jit.cpp_ext import get_cuda_version
+
+    version = get_cuda_version()
+    if (version.major, version.minor) < cl.LOCALITY_CUDA:
+        pytest.skip(f"Cake locality domains need a CUDA 13.5 toolkit, found {version}")
+    table = cl.sm_table(device)
+    if table is None:
+        pytest.skip("the device has no Cake SM table")
+    return device, table
+
+
+def _module():
+    from flashinfer.jit import env as jit_env
+    from flashinfer.jit.core import gen_jit_spec, sm107a_nvcc_flags
+    from flashinfer.jit.utils import write_if_different
+
+    name = "test_cake_locality_latency_chase"
+    source = jit_env.FLASHINFER_GEN_SRC_DIR / name / "chase.cu"
+    source.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    write_if_different(source, _CHASE_SOURCE)
+    spec = gen_jit_spec(
+        name, [source], extra_cuda_cflags=sm107a_nvcc_flags, use_fast_math=False
+    )
+    return spec.build_and_load()
+
+
+def test_locality_domain_is_the_lower_latency_die():
+    device, table = _require_table()
+    module = _module()
+    properties = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device)
+    sm_count = properties.multi_processor_count
+    l2_bytes = int(properties.L2_cache_size)
+    unit = cl.granularity(device)
+    # Each half spans twice the L2 and every CTA chases its own segment of it.
+    half_bytes = -(-2 * l2_bytes // unit) * unit
+    half_words = half_bytes // 4
+    nodes = half_words // STRIDE_WORDS
+    assert nodes // sm_count > STEPS
+    chain = cl.split_empty((2 * half_words,), torch.int32, half_bytes, device)
+    halves = chain.view(2, nodes, STRIDE_WORDS)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=f"cuda:{device}").manual_seed(1)
+    order = torch.randperm(
+        nodes, generator=generator, device=f"cuda:{device}", dtype=torch.int64
+    )
+    # The same random cycle over all nodes in both halves: node order[i] links to
+    # node order[i + 1].
+    halves[:, order, 0] = order.roll(-1).to(torch.int32)
+    starts = order[torch.arange(sm_count, device=order.device) * nodes // sm_count]
+    starts = starts.to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+    flush = torch.empty(2 * l2_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{device}")
+    out = torch.empty((sm_count, 6), dtype=torch.int64, device=f"cuda:{device}")
+
+    ns = {}  # smid -> ([ns of die 0], [ns of die 1])
+    domain_of = {}
+    for launch in range(2 * LAUNCHES):
+        for attempt in range(ATTEMPTS):
+            flush.fill_(launch + attempt)  # evict the chains from the L2
+            module.chase(chain, half_words, starts, STEPS, launch % 2, out)
+            rows = out.tolist()
+            if len({row[0] for row in rows}) == sm_count:
+                break
+        else:
+            pytest.fail(f"launch {launch} put no CTA on some SM in {ATTEMPTS} tries")
+        for smid, domain, _supplemental, ns0, ns1, _sink in rows:
+            assert domain in (0, 1), (smid, domain)
+            assert domain_of.setdefault(smid, domain) == domain, smid
+            times = ns.setdefault(smid, ([], []))
+            times[0].append(ns0)
+            times[1].append(ns1)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    del chain, halves
+
+    assert len(ns) == sm_count
+    counts = [0, 0]
+    ratios = {}
+    for smid, (die0, die1) in ns.items():
+        domain = domain_of[smid]
+        counts[domain] += 1
+        local = statistics.median((die0, die1)[domain])
+        remote = statistics.median((die0, die1)[1 - domain])
+        ratios[smid] = remote / local
+        word = int(table.entries[smid])
+        mask = (1 << cl.ENTRY_DOMAIN_BITS) - 1
+        table_domain = (word >> cl.ENTRY_DOMAIN_SHIFT) & mask
+        assert table_domain == domain, smid
+    print(
+        f"LOCALITY_LATENCY device={device} counts={counts} table={table.counts} "
+        f"remote_over_local min={min(ratios.values()):.3f} "
+        f"max={max(ratios.values()):.3f}"
+    )
+    assert tuple(counts) == tuple(table.counts)
+    slow = {
+        smid: round(ratio, 3)
+        for smid, ratio in ratios.items()
+        if ratio < MIN_REMOTE_OVER_LOCAL
+    }
+    assert not slow, f"SMs whose own die is not clearly nearer: {slow}"

# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"

      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
        id: cuda-versions
        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check Skip Conditions
        id: check
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 0
          fi

          # Use PR event SHAs for reliable diff (avoids issues with origin refs)
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
          # TODO (yongwww): Add back ^\.github/ before merging to main
          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"

          SKIP=true
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then

              break
            fi
          done <<< "$CHANGED"

      # matrix expands - a job-level `if` cannot see the matrix context, and

      - name: Build Test Matrix
        id: matrix
        env:
          SKIP_AOT: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_aot }}
          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
          # Targets requested by the triggering `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment,

          H100_ON_PRS: 'true'
